title: Variant Routing Guided Journey — staged traffic composer and rollback explainer
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design a guided composer for variant routing (canary, A/B, percentage splits) that focuses on progressive disclosure, safety hypotheses, and cost-aware traffic shaping. The prototype will show: 1) an onboarding microflow for first-time rollout authors, 2) a three-column composer (Variants / Traffic Timeline / Safety Gates) that supports drag-to-split and keyboard nudges, 3) an inline rollback explainer showing why an automatic rollback would trigger and what metrics are used, and 4) a compact diff timeline for comparing variant outputs and cost delta estimates. The goal is to give PMs and engineers confidence to run staged rollouts while making the cost and quality trade-offs explicit.
acceptance_criteria: Clickable Figma prototype covering onboarding, composer, timeline, and rollback explainer
Design spec with component list and micro-interaction details (keyboard nudges, drag handles, tooltips)
Handoff-ready tokens and spacing rules for dev (spacing, z-index guidance, color tokens)
Review feedback from Eng and PM addressed or captured as follow-ups
Accessibility checklist completed for core composer flows (keyboard, labels, color contrast)

decisions: Use progressive disclosure: hide cost details behind a collapsed panel by default, show estimated per-hour and per-100k-tokens on expand.
Rollback explainer will surface the top 3 signals (latency p95, error rate, quality regression score) and the exact threshold that would trigger automated rollback.
Min traffic split step is 0.5% with a 2% minimum for new variants (to avoid noisy micro-samples), enforced by UI affordances and validation.
Timeline uses 10-minute smoothing window for per-variant metrics to reduce churn from batch scheduling artifacts.
Cost delta is estimated using current model token rate and active batch size; values labeled as estimates with a link to the Optimize recommendations page.
